title: Five neutral backgrounds for edge-to-edge Block members
kicker: Member layout · Babble 5 · production winner deliberately unselected
brief: The production Block now has an Inset / Edge-to-edge structural switch. This separate study compares five background carriers for the Edge-to-edge state using the same Branch, members, and footer states; no candidate has been applied to production.
defaultWhy: Seam-only White is the provisional AI recommendation at 100/100: it leads every weighted criterion while adding no new notation. This is an advisory prune only; production remains visually neutral until Zach chooses.
decisionHinge: The recommendation hinges on hairline seams remaining visible at normal canvas zoom. If real usage shows they disappear, shifting 15 weight points from low visual weight to containment clarity makes Shared Recessed Well the safer direction.
invariants: Member layout remains a two-state Inset / Edge-to-edge structural control.
Member Blocks keep real boundaries, titles, hit targets, and direct membership.
The treatment composes with both shown and hidden member footers.
No candidate changes production code until Zach picks or explicitly accepts the provisional recommendation.
boundary: The gallery runs the layout and footer state machine in the real SystemSketch visual idiom; tldraw editing, persistence, wiring, and production theme switching remain simulated.

axes.name: Footer dependency
values: all five are explicitly exercised shown and hidden

requirements.name: Continuous-stack clarity
requirements.why: The Branch-like case should read as one solid structure at a glance.
requirements.passCondition: With Edge-to-edge selected, the two members share a clear continuous silhouette.

anchors.1: Still reads as two unrelated floating cards.
anchors.3: Reads as a stack after inspection.
anchors.5: Immediately reads as one container with internal members.

requirements.name: Member hierarchy without noise
requirements.why: Each function or arm must remain separately scannable without turning the board into a striped table.
requirements.passCondition: Both titles and boundaries are easy to follow while the background stays recessive.

anchors.1: Members blur together or the treatment dominates.
anchors.3: Boundaries are clear with some visual competition.
anchors.5: Members scan instantly and the treatment recedes.

requirements.name: Hidden-footer compatibility
requirements.why: Zach expects branch-like stacks to hide footers and still feel structurally complete.
requirements.passCondition: Turning footers off leaves intentional seams and no stranded bands.

anchors.1: The composition visibly depends on footers.
anchors.3: Still works but loses some rhythm.
anchors.5: Looks equally intentional with either footer state.

requirements.name: Theme robustness
requirements.why: SystemSketch uses host and canvas themes, so the treatment should be token-shaped rather than luminance-fragile.
requirements.passCondition: The design needs only existing surface and border roles and maintains contrast.

anchors.1: Depends on a brittle literal shade or low contrast.
anchors.5: Maps directly to existing semantic tokens.

requirements.name: Low visual weight
requirements.why: The background should support fast diagram reading rather than becoming a new notation.
requirements.passCondition: The treatment does not compete with ports, titles, or dataflow.

anchors.1: Adds a strong new pattern or accent.
anchors.5: Quiet enough to disappear during normal reading.

hardGates.name: Readable text
hardGates.why: Every title stays legible in shown and hidden-footer states.

hardGates.name: Visible member boundaries
hardGates.why: The if and else Blocks remain distinguishable without hover.

hardGates.name: No semantic color claim
hardGates.why: No treatment introduces an accent that could be mistaken for type, state, or flow meaning.

variants.name: Seam-only White
variants.thesis: Let structure do the work: one white silhouette, quiet one-pixel seams, and no background wash.
variants.bestWhen: Maximum neutrality matters and the existing border token already reads crisply.
variants.losesWhen: The canvas or display makes hairline separators hard to see.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: One-pixel seams between real child Blocks.

proof: All three state buttons drive the same stack.
Hiding footers leaves the existing member seam in place.

fr1.evidence: The outer Block and flush children form one uninterrupted white silhouette.

fr2.evidence: Titles and hairline seams scan without a competing fill pattern.

fr3.evidence: Footer removal exposes the same member-to-member seam, so rhythm is unchanged.

fr4.evidence: Only paper and border semantic roles are required.

fr5.evidence: Nothing new competes with ports, text, or dataflow.

g1.evidence: Black titles remain on white or very pale neutral surfaces in every state.

g2.evidence: A full-width border seam remains between if and else before and after footer removal.

g3.evidence: The prototype uses only neutral surface roles; no accent suggests status or type.

variants.name: Shared Recessed Well
variants.thesis: Place the whole stack on a continuous recessed bed so membership is read from containment rather than stripes.
variants.bestWhen: The parent needs a little more separation from member surfaces on large sparse canvases.
variants.losesWhen: The five-pixel edge reveal feels like an accidental gutter at small zoom levels.

decisions.label: Tone carrier
decisions.value: One continuous gray bed behind every member.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Shared containment with a narrow edge reveal.

proof: The well persists under both members as one continuous plane.
Footer hiding does not strand any tone band.

fr1.evidence: A continuous recessed plane visibly belongs to the parent rather than either member.

fr2.evidence: The edge reveal clarifies containment but adds a second boundary beside each member.

fr3.evidence: The parent bed is independent of footer height and remains complete when footers disappear.

fr4.evidence: Paper, quiet surface, and border roles map directly to theme tokens.

fr5.evidence: The treatment is neutral, though more visible than the seam-only control.

g1.evidence: Black titles remain on white or very pale neutral surfaces in every state.

g2.evidence: Member seams remain visible over the parent-owned well in every state.

g3.evidence: The prototype uses only neutral surface roles; no accent suggests status or type.

variants.name: Alternating Body Bands
variants.thesis: Alternate pale member surfaces to make branch arms instantly traceable down a longer stack.
variants.bestWhen: A parent may contain many similar members and row tracking is the dominant need.
variants.losesWhen: Only two or three members are common, where zebra rhythm reads heavier than the content.
proof: The same if member stays tinted with and without its footer.
Inset mode demonstrates that alternation is independent of geometry.

fr1.evidence: Alternation binds the stack, though the two different surfaces slightly weaken the single-silhouette read.

fr2.evidence: Each member is very easy to follow, but the striped rhythm competes with the titles.

fr3.evidence: A band belongs to the whole member and therefore survives footer removal cleanly.

fr4.evidence: Two neutral surface tokens work across themes but require careful contrast tuning.

fr5.evidence: Zebra striping is the most noticeable and notation-like candidate.

g1.evidence: Black titles remain on white or very pale neutral surfaces in every state.

g2.evidence: Alternating full-member surfaces keep both child boundaries legible without hover.

g3.evidence: The prototype uses only neutral surface roles; no accent suggests status or type.

variants.name: Header Wash
variants.thesis: Tint only each child header, turning titles into quiet section bars while leaving content on paper.
variants.bestWhen: Member titles are the main scan path and bodies can be visually sparse.
variants.losesWhen: A stack already has many labeled bands, where another header layer feels nested and busy.
proof: Both member names anchor a stable pale bar.
Removing footers has no effect on the header-based hierarchy.

fr1.evidence: Flush members still share one outer shape, though repeated bars subdivide it strongly.

fr2.evidence: Names and boundaries are immediate without tinting the data-bearing body.

fr3.evidence: The grouping cue lives entirely in headers, so footer removal is lossless.

fr4.evidence: The treatment uses the same quiet header surface role as existing chrome.

fr5.evidence: The wash stays pale and localized, but introduces more horizontal bands.

g1.evidence: Black titles remain on white or very pale neutral surfaces in every state.

g2.evidence: Each washed header begins a visibly separate member and a seam closes it below.

g3.evidence: The prototype uses only neutral surface roles; no accent suggests status or type.

variants.name: Inset Body Field
variants.thesis: Keep member frames flush, but recess only their content fields to create depth inside one continuous stack.
variants.bestWhen: Member bodies contain rich material that benefits from a distinct working surface.
variants.losesWhen: Bodies are mostly empty, where the nested field looks decorative or like an input control.

decisions.label: Tone carrier
decisions.value: A rounded field inside each member body.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Depth within members rather than between them.

proof: The body fields respond to footer removal without leaving extra bands.
Inset mode shows the intentional nested-card cost.

fr1.evidence: The outer stack remains joined, but inner rounded fields weaken its flat continuous character.

fr2.evidence: Each title/body pair is clear, though the body boxes can resemble form inputs.

fr3.evidence: Footer hiding still produces complete body fields with intentional bottom spacing.

fr4.evidence: Neutral body and border roles are portable with moderate token tuning.

fr5.evidence: Localized depth is quieter than zebra bands but heavier than seams or header wash.

g1.evidence: Black titles remain on white or very pale neutral surfaces in every state.

g2.evidence: Full-width member seams remain visible even though body content gains its own field.

g3.evidence: The prototype uses only neutral surface roles; no accent suggests status or type.
